spec_cite: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §5.2 (AUTHENTICATING: supersede — the older session of the same identity is closed with Close(303))
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §10 (one active session per Client identity, TM-3)
description: Same-identity supersede: a second connection authenticates the same Client identity; the OLD connection is closed with Close(303) (Close only — the §5.2 row names no paired Error).
preconditions: Connection A: established, authenticated (session_id 1), state PLAYING.
Connection B: fresh CONNECTING -> AUTHENTICATING for the same identity; the auth exchange there consumed request_id 1.

steps.note: On connection B: the new session is accepted (session_id 2).
On connection A: the superseded session is closed.

assertions: The old session's Close is unsolicited from A's perspective; Close is one-way and never echoed (spec §5.4).
retryable=false per §6.2: another session owns this identity — the Client surfaces it, no automatic reconnect (spec §6.3).
Supersede replaces, not rejects: the replacement is counted in diagnostics (TM-3).
The §5.2 row names Close(303) alone (no paired Error) — this vector shows exactly that.
